subject: Invoice delivery and billing-contact setup: email PDF vs portal API onboarding
messages:
From: Jordan Price <j.price@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, AP Team <ap.ar@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice delivery options and PO flow

Hi Ben,

We are gearing up for production usage and need to finalize how invoices will be sent to ACME's AP team. Our treasury prefers either: (1) a standard PDF emailed to ap.ar@acme-corp.com with PO number on the subject and remittance details in the body, or (2) an automated push into our vendor portal via an API (preferred for volume).

A couple of constraints on our side:
- VAT/Tax block: copies of invoices must show VAT breakdown and be locked for edits once issued.
- We require PO matching on the invoice header (PO visible in filename and metadata).
- We need an initial 2-week pilot for about ~50 invoices to validate EDI/API mapping before full cutover.

Can Redwood support both paths? If so, what's the quickest path to enable the portal API push? Otherwise we'll default to PDF-by-email for now.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Finance Operations – ACME Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <j.price@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery options and PO flow

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Short answer: yes, we can do both.

Options we typically offer:
- Email PDF: Redwood can send signed PDF invoices to a specified address. We include PO number in subject and filename. This is the fastest to turn on (hours) and good for low-volume customers.
- SFTP/Flat-file drop: nightly batch of CSVs plus PDFs if you prefer one-time setup and your AP team wants files landed to a secure SFTP.
- API push (preferred for scale): our Billing service can push invoice payloads (JSON) to a customer endpoint or into your portal via a vendor API. This requires a one-time schema mapping and a short test harness.

Tax/VAT details: all invoice templates include VAT line items and tax IDs by default. When we issue an invoice we can set a "finalized" flag so edits are prevented and a signed PDF stored. For legal lock we recommend the API push to also send the signed PDF as an attachment, so both metadata and human-readable invoice are captured.

Pilot plan for API push (typical timeline):
1) Schema review & mapping (1–2 business days) — we attached an example mapping sheet.
2) Test endpoint + 10 sample invoices (2–3 days).
3) Pilot at ~50 invoices over 2 weeks.
4) Cutover and monitoring.

I've attached our invoice_spec.xlsx with the JSON/CSV mapping for your portal. To proceed with API onboarding we'll need:
- A test endpoint and a service account key for Redwood to push to (or API docs for your portal).
- PO matching rules (exact filename/metadata requirements).
- Confirmation whether Redwood should be the billing contact or if invoices should be sent directly to your AP mailbox.

If you need a faster fallback we can enable email-PDF delivery immediately while we stand up the API pilot. 

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0149

We'll provide a test endpoint by end of day Tuesday and will send credentials in a secure team message. For the short term, please start sending PDFs to ap.ar@acme-corp.com as a fallback so our AP doesn't stall.

Jordan
